newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel destroys two tunnels linking Gaza, Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Israel destroys two tunnels linking Gaza, Egypt.

text.p: The Israeli army on Sunday blew up two tunnels it said were dug illicitly by Palestinians for smuggling weapons from Egypt to the Gaza Strip.
"The tunnels were exploded today. The army is investigating if weapons were transferred through the tunnels that were exposed," an army spokesman said.
He said the soldiers discovered the tunnels, linking the Egyptian and Palestinian sides of the border town Rafah, during a search along Israel's southern border with Egypt.

"This tunnel (here) is about four and a half metres (15 feet) deep and it's big enough for a medium-sized person to pass through it," said an army commander who could be identified only as Colonel Lior.
"I have almost no doubt that in the Palestinian Authority they know about its existence," he told reporters.
Palestinian officials have denied tunnels are used to smuggle weapons and said Israel refused to let them see the tunnels.
"I don't think it's true," said Colonel Khaled Abu-Ola, commander of the Palestinian liaison office in southern Gaza.
The Palestinian Authority controls most of the Gaza Strip under a 1993 peace deal that left Israel in charge of overall security and border crossings.

Israel first found tunnels linking Gaza and Egypt in 1993, the same year it reached its landmark accord with the PLO. At the time the tunnels were used to smuggle food, weapons and wanted Palestinians in and out of Gaza, the army said.
Since then, Egyptian and Israeli security forces have found and destroyed more than 12 tunnels linking Rafah's two halves.
